title: Understanding SVD
text: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) is a method of decomposing a matrix into three other matrices: $X=USV**{T}$. Here, $U$ and $V$ are orthogonal matrices, and $S$ is a diagonal matrix containing singular values.

title: Rank and Singular Values
text: The rank of a matrix is the number of non-zero singular values in its SVD. If $rank(X)<d$, what does this imply about the diagonal matrix $S$?

hintAnswer: There must be at least one $$0$$ along the diagonal of $S$.
title: Diagonal of $S$
text: Given that $rank(X)<d$, what can we say about the diagonal elements of $S$?
choices: There must be at least one $$0$$ along the diagonal of $S$.
